I planned on saving for a sound card and getting it the holiday season, along with a quality pair of headphones. Thank you for the alternate build.

Don't get a soundcard, get a DAC (digital to analog converter) instead.

Soundcards are outdated, and just get a lot of interference from the PC components. DACs being outside of the computer will receive much less interference at the same price.

If you're thinking about getting a nice set of headphones to use along with a pc, think about getting an external dac and amp. An internal sound card might not be strong enough to push some headphones that have around 250 - 600 ohms and also you could very well get electrical noise from the sound card being inside the case. Just a thought.

If it's a general purpose machine that you intend to use as your main gaming rig, then I recommend going with a gaming video card instead of a workstation video card. That's because you're probably going to be less bothered by longer waiting times on whatever it is you plan on rendering than having to deal with low frame rates in video games (workstation gpus are faster with professional 3d applications but slower for gaming).
